lines.text: Nine low islands in the Pacific, a British colony, a tiny nation and a rising sea. This is the story of Tuvalu.
Long settled by Polynesian voyagers, the Ellice Islands were ruled by Britain together with the Gilberts as one colony from 1916.
Toaripi Lauti, born in 1928, would become the new nation's first prime minister.
Enele Sopoaga, born in 1956, would lead the country from 2013 to 2019.
Kausea Natano, born a year later, would follow him as prime minister until 2024.
And Feleti Teo, born in 1962, would become prime minister in 2024.
In 1974 the Ellice Islanders voted to separate from the Gilberts and go their own way.
In 1978 Tuvalu became independent, one of the smallest countries in the world.
In 1996 it was given its internet address, dot T V, which it rents out to television and streaming companies.
In 2023, with the sea rising around its islands, Tuvalu signed a treaty under which Australia offers its people a new home.
A small nation with a large voice, Tuvalu keeps warning the world about the rising sea.
